panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is axial T2-weighted abdominal MRI from juvenile hemochromatosis case showing diffuse hypointense liver and pancreas signals with preserved splenic signal, described as characteristic of primary hemochromatosis. B: Panel B is out-of-phase T1 abdominal MRI showing same diffuse hepatic and pancreatic iron deposition pattern characteristic of primary hemochromatosis. C: Panel C is in-phase T1 abdominal MRI showing progressive signal loss in liver and pancreas relative to out-of-phase, confirming multi-organ iron deposition with preserved splenic signal characteristic of primary hemochromatosis.

panels.figure_caption: Abdominal MRI performed to assess parenchymal iron burden shows axial T2-weighted (A), out-of-phase T1 (B), and in-phase T1 (C) sequences. Diffusely decreased signal intensity is present in the liver (solid arrow) and pancreas (dashed arrow) across all sequences, with progressive signal loss on in-phase relative to out-of-phase T1, consistent with hepatic and pancreatic iron deposition. Splenic signal is preserved, a pattern characteristic of primary hemochromatosis. Qualitative MRI assessment of parenchymal iron burden is a noninvasive tool that can confirm multi-organ iron deposition before irreversible end-organ damage occurs. Its early use in young patients with unexplained hypogonadism or atypical diabetes could facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention.
